% Framework figure of the improved FedCLEAR (gatef). Generated by tools/plot_framework.py.
% Copy clear_v2_framework.pdf next to samplepaper.tex (e.g. into Figs/) and paste the block below.
\begin{figure}[t]
    \centering
    \includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{Figs/clear_v2_framework.pdf}
    \caption{Overview of FedCLEAR. In every round the server broadcasts the global prompt
    $\mathbf{v}^r$. Each client computes the reference prediction $\mathbf{P}_i$ (the global prompt
    averaged with zero-shot CLIP), flags itself when its mean excess surprise $S_k$ exceeds $\tau$,
    marks suspect samples, relabels or sets them aside, and trains its prompt on the repaired data;
    the server averages the prompts, weighted by the repaired data sizes. After round $R$ a
    referee-strength gate decides once whether the reference prediction is reliable enough for
    calibrated repair: it opens when the one-sided 95\% Wilson lower bound of the share of suspects
    that could be relabelled is at least $g$. Once the gate is open (orange), the server fits one
    temperature $T \le 1$ per round from the clients' profile log-likelihoods $\ell_k(t)$, and a
    flagged client marks as suspects the samples whose label lies outside the 95\% prediction set of
    $\mathbf{P}^T$, and at least $\varepsilon^0_k n_k$ of them, where $\varepsilon^0_k$ is its own
    noise estimate frozen at the first calibrated round. While the gate is closed, the standard rule
    is used (white). We use $\tau = 0.05$, $\delta = 0.1$, $\gamma = 0.6$, $\kappa = 0.5$,
    $\alpha = 0.05$, $g = 0.12$ and $R = 5$.}
    \label{fig:framework}
\end{figure}
